Q: What is a physical network diagram?
Option1: A map of subnets and routing domains
Option2: A drawing that shows real devices, racks, and cabling routes and terminations
Option3: A list of IP address assignments

Q: What is a logical network diagram?
Option1: A map of physical cable trays and rack elevations
Option2: A conceptual view showing subnets, virtual local area networks, routing, and traffic flows

Q: Which diagram most commonly shows exact cable types and port IDs?
Option2: Layer 2 network diagram

Q: Which diagram is best for showing virtual local area networks and switch trunks?
Option2: Layer 2 network diagram

Q: Which diagram is best for showing IP subnets and routing between them?
Option2: Layer 2 network diagram

Q: What does a rack diagram capture?
Option2: The front view of mounted equipment with rack unit positions, dimensions, and dependencies

Q: What is a cable map or diagram used for?
Option2: Documenting cable paths, endpoints, labels, and patch-panel mappings

Q: What is asset inventory in networking?
Option2: A complete record of hardware, software, licensing, and warranty/support details

Q: What is Internet Protocol Address Management (IPAM)?
Option1: A replacement for Domain Name System servers
Option2: A system/process to plan, allocate, track, and audit Internet Protocol addresses and integrate with Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol and Domain Name System

Q: What is a service-level agreement (SLA)?
Option2: A contract defining measurable service targets such as uptime and response time
Option4: A security policy for passwords only

Q: What is a wireless survey/heat map?
Option1: A tool for measuring power distribution in racks
Option2: A visualization of signal strength, interference, and coverage to guide access point placement

Q: What does end-of-life (EOL) indicate?
Option1: The vendor still sells the product but stops updates
Option2: The vendor stops selling new units; limited or no updates going forward

Q: What does end-of-support (EOS) indicate?
Option1: The vendor will continue firmware patches indefinitely
Option2: The vendor no longer provides fixes or assistance, which increases operational risk
Option3: The vendor provides extended warranties automatically

Q: Which falls under software management in life-cycle management?
Option1: Patches and bug fixes, operating system updates, and firmware updates
Option2: Only power supplies

Q: What is decommissioning?
Option2: Securely retiring assets, including configuration backup, data sanitization, and proper disposal

Q: What is change management in networking?
Option2: A controlled process for requesting, approving, implementing, and documenting changes

Q: What is a production configuration?
Option1: A lab template for future builds
Option2: The active, running configuration on a device providing service

Q: What is a backup configuration?
Option2: A stored copy of device configuration for recovery and audit purposes

Q: What is a baseline or golden configuration?
Option1: The worst-performing config kept for history
Option2: A known-good, approved standard configuration used for comparison and drift detection

Q: Why keep a baseline plus backups?
Option1: It eliminates the need for approvals
Option2: To compare current settings to a standard and to restore quickly after failures or bad changes

Q: Which documentation best helps a technician trace a failed copper link from desk to switch port?
Option2: Cable map with patch-panel mappings and labeling scheme

Q: Which document helps plan capacity for a refresh cycle by warranty status?
Option2: Asset inventory including warranty support dates
